recent_posts.title: How WP Engine uses Elastic and Google Cloud to power search for 2 million users
recent_posts.summary: WP Engine partnered with Elastic and Google Cloud to deliver high-precision search for over 2 million users. The unified architecture combines Elastic's search capabilities natively built on Google Cloud Platform, enabling near-instant content updates (as low as 5ms response times), zero-downtime scaling, and rapid AI feature deployment. Elastic's native grounding within Vertex AI allows WP Engine customers to build generative AI applications and conversational interfaces powered by real-time vector search over proprietary content.

recent_posts.title: The agentic era: Elastic at Google Cloud Next 2026
recent_posts.summary: Elastic recaps its presence at Google Cloud Next 2026, highlighting several joint announcements: being named Google Cloud Partner of the Year for the fifth time, becoming an embedded security layer for Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped environments, making Jina Embeddings v3 available on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Model Garden, launching a CPU-optimized Arm hardware profile powered by Google Axion processors (delivering up to 25% better price-performance), and announcing native Prometheus and PromQL support in Elastic Observability. Additional sessions covered AI architectures on Cloud Run, the Elastic Agent Builder and Workflows tools, and Google Cloud ADC integration.

recent_posts.title: Elastic 9.4: Workflows GA, Agent Builder updates, and Prometheus/PromQL support
recent_posts.summary: Elastic 9.4 is now generally available, bringing major updates across the Elasticsearch Platform, Observability, and Security products. Key highlights include: Elastic Workflows reaching GA for automation and agentic orchestration; Agent Builder gaining Skills, Attachments, Connectors, and Plugins; native Prometheus and PromQL support with Elasticsearch TSDB claimed to be 2.6x more storage-efficient and 25x faster than Prometheus; GPU-accelerated vector indexing via NVIDIA cuVS now GA with up to 12x indexing throughput improvement; ES|QL gaining subqueries, approximate queries, logical views, and access to unmapped fields; AI-powered dashboard creation in Kibana; FIPS 140-3 compliance for both Elasticsearch and Kibana; and four new Entity Analytics capabilities for security teams including Precision Entity Identification and Entity Resolution.

recent_posts.title: How IT leaders can measure the ROI of agentic AI initiatives
recent_posts.summary: As organizations scale agentic AI beyond pilots, traditional ROI models fall short because AI agents are nondeterministic — costs and outputs vary with each task. IT leaders need a new financial framework that accounts for variable token consumption, hidden costs like integration and change management, and nuanced value metrics. Key proposed metrics include Agent Value Multiple (AVM), Agent Cost per Completed Task (ACCT), Context Memory Optimization Score (CMOS), and Effective Context Utilization (ECU). Before deployment, establishing a human baseline for process times and error rates is essential. Hidden costs to budget for include application maintenance, legacy system integration, security/governance frameworks, data management, and organizational change management.

recent_posts.title: Public sector AI: 5 shifts driving mission outcomes
recent_posts.summary: Public sector organizations are shifting AI use from individual productivity tools to end-to-end agentic workflows. Key trends include significant IT budget reallocation toward AI (65% of agencies planning 11%+ of IT budget), a move from 'human in the loop' to 'human in the lead' governance models, the need for open and modular data architectures to avoid vendor lock-in, and growing adoption of sovereign AI to control data residency and access. IDC survey data from 152 federal entities shows 80% expect measurable ROI within 12 months and 46% already use some form of sovereign AI.

recent_posts.title: Built on patterns: How Susan Chang’s econometrics roots drive machine learning for security and her minimalist workspace
recent_posts.summary: Susan Chang, a principal data scientist at Elastic's Security team, shares how her econometrics background shaped her approach to machine learning for cybersecurity. She builds ML systems that detect anomalous behavior in high-volume security data streams, including evaluation frameworks to measure model improvements and reduce false positives. The post also covers her minimalist desk setup and her advice for those entering security ML: build strong ML fundamentals first, then learn the domain.

recent_posts.title: Whole-of-state cyber defense: How AI-driven security helps US states protect what matters most
recent_posts.summary: US state and local governments face growing cyber threats complicated by uneven security resources across agencies. A whole-of-state cybersecurity model addresses this by enabling shared threat visibility, coordinated incident response, and collective resilience without forcing data centralization. Distributed architectures allow agencies to retain data sovereignty while participating in statewide defense. AI-driven security analytics act as a force multiplier for understaffed teams by automating alert triage, guided investigation, and faster response. Context engineering ensures AI outputs are grounded in verified, policy-compliant local data, preventing hallucinations and protecting sensitive citizen information. The approach aligns with the March 2026 National Cyber Strategy for America and CISA frameworks, aiming to extend elite security capabilities to under-resourced entities like K-12 districts and small municipalities.

recent_posts.title: State of Observability in Financial Services 2026
recent_posts.summary: A 2026 research report from Elastic on observability trends in financial services reveals that 70% of IT leaders now classify their practices as mature or expert, up from 45% a year ago. Key findings include 94% GenAI adoption for observability, a stark gap where 89% expect LLM observability but only 6% have implemented it, OpenTelemetry production usage tripling to 10%, and 95% of organizations facing regulatory compliance challenges. Cost optimization is near-universal with 99% of organizations taking active steps to reduce observability spending. The report also highlights that observability data is expanding beyond IT, with 67% of cybersecurity teams relying on it for threat detection.

recent_posts.title: Google Axion-powered Arm hardware profiles now available on Elastic Cloud
recent_posts.summary: Elastic Cloud Hosted now offers a new CPU-optimized (Arm) hardware profile powered by Google Axion, Google's custom Arm-based processors. The new profile delivers up to 25% better price-performance compared to the previous CPU-optimized generation, benefiting search, observability, and security workloads. Both new deployments and existing deployments can use the profile via the Elastic Cloud console with a few straightforward steps. The profile is available in select Google Cloud regions.

recent_posts.title: Securing air-gapped environments with Elastic on Google Distributed Cloud
recent_posts.summary: Elastic Security is now the embedded security layer for Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) air-gapped environments, bringing AI-driven defense to government, defense, finance, and telecom organizations operating fully disconnected from the public internet. The integration unifies SIEM, XDR, and native automation in a single platform, with kernel-level endpoint protection via Elastic Defend, AI-powered attack discovery using on-premises Gemini models, and native workflow automation (replacing standalone SOAR). Key benefits include model sovereignty — AI capabilities run locally without requiring cloud connectivity — and no per-endpoint pricing for Elastic Defend. The announcement follows Elastic's December 2025 SIEM-as-a-Service partnership with CISA for US federal agencies.
